# Resend

Authenticated by `RESEND_API_KEY`, injected from 1Password at launch. Never
put the key on a command line as a value.

Confirm auth before anything else:

```bash
curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $RESEND_API_KEY" https://api.resend.com/domains \
  | jq -r '.data[] | "\(.name)\t\(.status)\t\(.region)"'
```

## Reading — safe, use freely

```bash
H="Authorization: Bearer $RESEND_API_KEY"
curl -fsS -H "$H" https://api.resend.com/domains/<id>     # records and their status
curl -fsS -H "$H" https://api.resend.com/emails/<id>      # one email: last_event
curl -fsS -H "$H" https://api.resend.com/api-keys         # names only, never values
```

## "The user never got the email"

1. Find the id: the app logs it from the send response, `data.id`.
2. `GET /emails/<id>` → `last_event`:

| `last_event` | Where the problem is |
|---|---|
| `delivered` | the recipient's inbox or spam. Not Resend, not the app |
| `bounced` | the address — read `bounce.type`; a hard bounce will never deliver |
| `complained` | marked as spam by the recipient; stop sending to them |
| `delivery_delayed` | the receiving server; Resend retries |
| `sent`, `queued` | in flight; check again |

3. No id at all → the send failed before Resend accepted it. That error is in
   the app's logs, and the codes below say what it means.

## Diagnosing a send error

| Resend said | It means |
|---|---|
| `validation_error … domain is not verified` | verify the domain: `GET /domains/<id>` shows which DNS record is missing |
| `restricted_api_key` | a sending-only key is being used for a read |
| `invalid_from_address` | the `from` is not on a verified domain |
| `rate_limit_exceeded` | 2 requests per second by default; batch instead |

## Never without asking

Anything that sends or changes DNS expectations:

```
POST /emails, /emails/batch      # sends real mail to real people
POST /domains, DELETE /domains/<id>
POST /domains/<id>/verify         # harmless, but say so
DELETE /api-keys/<id>
```

A test send is fine to an address the human names. Never to a real user.
